items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters provided an overview of the County’s Solid Waste Management initiatives and waste diversion strategy, including the implementation of a minimum waste fee at transfer stations. He also provided highlights of the County’s Newcomer tour and reception.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Councillor Wilton highlighted recent events in Fergus including the Clogs and Clockwork event and the Twilight at Templin Gardens.

items.title: Daniel Segal, Segal Construction (via zoom)
notes: re: Municipal Residential Development of Attainable Housing D. Segal, Segal Construction proposed a partnership to provide attainable housing that is funded through a mix of municipal bonds and federal/provincial funding. He noted this approach leverages the municipality's low cost of capital to create attainable housing and once complete, Council can choose to sell the units on the open market, manage them directly, or transfer them to affordable housing providers.
Mayor Watters thanked D. Segal for his presentation and after a brief discussion, the following was put forward:

items.title: Introduction of Artist - Michael Madden
notes: Barb Lee from the Elora Fergus Arts Council introduced local artist Michael Madden. Michael Madden highlighted the inspiration for his rural landscapes.

items.title: MacLean Hann, Chair Elora BIA spoke in support of the staff proposal
notes: regarding item 11.6 Tourism Washroom Project Update and the modification of the design to include Molok containers to address the mounting garbage problem in downtown Elora. He outlined the concerns with the amount of garbage generated, the insufficient weekly pick-up system and the lack of storage for garbage. He responded to questions regarding the amount of garbage generated and efforts taken to reduce that amount.

items.title: Randy Vaine
notes: re: 11.8 Termite Management Update
Randy Vaine, resident spoke regarding item 11.8 Termite Management Update. He expressed concerns with the potential spread of termites.

He highlighted the City of Guelph’s program and the belief they have eradicated termites. He suggested the Township consult with the City of Guelph and actively enforce the Township’s termite by-law. He also suggested the Township implement an education program.

items.title: Maria Creco-O’Neill, Elora Fergus Termites appeared before Council in
notes: support of the termite subsidy program as a starting point. She suggested the Township support termite management and eradication efforts by assisting with wood and soil removal, identify designated termite management zones with tracking and monitoring, the treatment of public spaces, free burn permits, etc.

items.title: John Kears and Renata Carter appeared in opposition to the
notes: recommendation in item 11.6 Tourism Washroom Project Update with the proposed inclusion of the installation of Molok garbage containers adjacent to the proposed washrooms and their property. He indicated there was no consultation undertaken, they were unaware of the proposal and respectfully requested an alternative location be considered.

Geoffry Wild, owner of the Badley and Wild Tart, 61 Metcalfe Street appeared in support of the Molok garbage system but does not support the proposed location. He believes more consultation should take place to seek solutions to reduce the amount of garbage and find storage suitable for all businesses.
Mayor Watters called a 5 minute recess.

items.title: Consent Items
notes: Mayor Watters indicated the Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. Any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate action.

Councillor MacDonald asked the minutes from the May 27, 2024 Council meeting be removed from the consent agenda. She proposed an amendment to include the following statement be added, “An invitation was extended to the original delegation, indicating the subject of Cannabis would be under consideration at the May 27th meeting.”

notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report and responded to questions and comments regarding priority setting, youth appointments to advisory committees, and implementation of a community planning permit system.

items.title: Tourism Washroom Project Update
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services Kasey Beirnes, Building and Facilities Project Manager provided an overview of the proposal to include molok garbage containers adjacent to the proposed washroom building on East Mill Street. He outlined the current challenges and struggles with the garbage and recycling in downtown Elora and noted installation of the moloks would be the first step in finding a solution to the garbage issues.
Staff responded to questions regarding the project timeline, consultation with the BIA and what other locations were considered.

items.title: Green Space Donation for Improvements Agreement
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services Lucas Rogerson, Manager of Parks outlined the landscaping plan for the Green Space improvements, including installation of the stone steps from Francis Lane, removal of the existing pond, installation of an additional garbage bin, and removal of two Norway Maple trees. He responded to questions regarding the donor funding, consultation undertaken, planting of new trees, and inclusion of a U hedge.

items.title: Termite Management Update
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report, indicating staff is seeking Council direction regarding the Township’s involvement in termite management services. He indicated staff are recommending the development of a subsidy style program to support property owners with termite mitigation strategies with the aim to significantly reduce the termite population in Centre Wellington.
